name: Goan Fish Curry
cuisine: Goan (Konkan coast; in Goa it is the everyday "xitt kodi" of fish curry rice, cooked in almost every Catholic and Hindu home; close cousins are Malvani fish curry and Karwari/Mangalorean gassi)

ingredients.name: Seer fish (surmai / kingfish), steaks, skin and bone on
Fresh grated coconut (nariyal), or frozen grated coconut, thawed
Kashmiri dried red chillies (sukhi lal mirch)
Onion (pyaz/kanda)
ingredients.householdMeasure: ½ small onion, finely chopped (about 4 tbsp)

ingredients.name: Water, to adjust the curry
ingredients.householdMeasure: ½ cup (less if you like it thick)

equipment: Mixer-grinder with a small chutney jar
Small dry pan (tadka pan or small kadai) for roasting the whole spices
Medium heavy-bottomed kadai or wide pan, about 20 cm (a wide pan lets the fish sit in one layer)
2 small bowls (kokum soak, fish marinade) and a plate
Measuring spoons and a measuring cup (normal teaspoons and a steel glass are fine stand-ins)
Kitchen scale (useful for the fish; or ask the fish seller for 150 g, which is about 2 medium steaks)

steps.title: Soak the kokum
steps.text: Put 3 pieces (5 g) kokum in a small bowl with 2 tbsp (30 ml) warm water.
steps.tip: Using tamarind instead? Soak 5 g tamarind the same way.
steps.visualCue: The water starts turning pinkish-purple within a few minutes.
steps.cameraCheck: The kokum in its bowl of water
steps.videoShot: Dark kokum pieces dropping into warm water.

steps.title: Rinse the fish
steps.text: Rinse the 150 g surmai steaks under cold running water and place them on a plate.
steps.tip: Frozen fish must be fully thawed first (see Quick facts). Ask the fish seller to cut steaks about 1.5 cm thick; thin steaks break in the curry.
steps.visualCue: No blood or scales on the surface
steps.cameraCheck: The 2 steaks on the plate
steps.videoShot: Water running over the steaks.

steps.title: Pat the fish dry
steps.text: Press both sides of each steak with a paper towel or clean cloth.
steps.visualCue: The surface looks matte, not wet
steps.cameraCheck: The dried steaks
steps.videoShot: The towel pressing on a steak.

steps.title: Marinate the fish
steps.text: Rub ⅛ tsp turmeric, a pinch of salt and 1 tsp lime juice over both sides. Set aside.
steps.tip: Do not marinate in lime for more than 30 minutes; the acid starts to "cook" the surface and makes it mushy.
steps.visualCue: Evenly yellow steaks
steps.cameraCheck: The marinated steaks on the plate
steps.videoShot: Fingers rubbing turmeric over a steak.

steps.title: Heat the small pan
steps.text: Put the small dry pan on low to medium heat.
steps.visualCue: Warm air rises when you hold your palm 5 cm above it
steps.cameraCheck: The empty pan on the flame
steps.videoShot: A hand hovering over the pan.

steps.title: Dry-roast the chillies
steps.text: Add the 3 Kashmiri chillies, stalks removed, and stir.
steps.tip: Burnt chillies make the curry bitter. If any turn black, throw them out.
steps.visualCue: They puff slightly, turn a shade brighter and become crisp. Not black.
steps.cameraCheck: The roasted chillies in the pan
steps.videoShot: Chillies being turned in the pan.

steps.title: Add the seeds and pepper
steps.text: Add 1 tsp coriander seeds, ¼ tsp cumin seeds and 4 peppercorns. Stir.
steps.visualCue: The coriander seeds turn a shade darker and the kitchen smells toasty
steps.cameraCheck: The spices in the pan
steps.videoShot: Seeds being stirred with a spoon.

steps.title: Cool the spices
steps.text: Tip the roasted spices onto a plate.
steps.visualCue: Cool to touch
steps.cameraCheck: The spices on the plate
steps.videoShot: Spices tumbling onto the plate.

steps.title: Grind the spices dry
steps.text: Put the cooled spices in the small chutney jar and grind without water.
steps.tip: Grinding the dry spices first gives a smoother final paste.
steps.visualCue: A coarse red-brown powder
steps.cameraCheck: The powder in the open jar
steps.videoShot: The jar lid lifted to show the powder.

steps.title: Peel the garlic and ginger
steps.text: Peel 2 garlic cloves (6 g) and a ½-inch piece of ginger (3 g).
steps.visualCue: Clean cloves and a peeled ginger piece
steps.cameraCheck: The garlic and ginger on the board
steps.videoShot: A spoon edge scraping the ginger skin.

steps.title: Add the coconut and aromatics to the jar
steps.text: Add 40 g (⅓ cup) grated coconut, the garlic, ginger, a pinch of turmeric and 3 tbsp (about 45 ml) of the grinding water.
steps.tip: Coconut milk shortcut: skip the coconut here, grind the spices, garlic and ginger with the water only, and keep 60 ml coconut milk ready for step 22.
steps.visualCue: Coconut, aromatics and a little water over the spice powder
steps.cameraCheck: The loaded jar, lid off
steps.videoShot: Coconut being added to the jar.

steps.title: Grind to a smooth paste
steps.text: Grind, scrape down the sides, add the remaining water (about 35 ml) and grind again.
steps.visualCue: A smooth, bright orange-red paste with no visible coconut shreds when rubbed between fingers
steps.cameraCheck: The paste on a spoon
steps.videoShot: The spoon lifting thick orange paste out of the jar.

steps.title: Chop the onion
steps.text: Finely chop 40 g onion (about ½ small onion). Slit 1 green chilli lengthwise.
steps.visualCue: Small, even onion pieces; chilli split but still joined at the stalk
steps.cameraCheck: The onion and chilli on the board
steps.videoShot: The knife rocking through the onion.

steps.title: Heat the oil
steps.text: Put the kadai on medium heat and add 2 tsp (10 ml) coconut oil.
steps.visualCue: The oil shimmers and flows easily when you tilt the pan
steps.cameraCheck: The oil in the pan
steps.videoShot: Oil swirling in the tilted kadai.

steps.title: Cook the onion
steps.text: Add the onion and green chilli. Stir now and then.
steps.tip: Adding the optional tomato? Add it now and cook 2 more minutes until soft.
steps.visualCue: Soft, translucent onion with light-golden edges
steps.cameraCheck: The onion in the pan
steps.videoShot: The spatula stirring the softened onion.

steps.title: Add the masala paste
steps.text: Lower the heat to low-medium and add all the ground paste. Rinse the jar with 2 tbsp of the 100 ml curry water and add that too.
steps.visualCue: The pan is full of thick orange-red paste
steps.cameraCheck: The paste in the pan
steps.videoShot: Paste being scraped into the kadai.

steps.title: Cook the paste
steps.text: Stir often so it does not catch.
steps.tip: If it sticks, add 1 tbsp water and keep stirring.
steps.visualCue: The raw garlic smell goes, the paste darkens slightly and tiny drops of oil appear at the edges
steps.cameraCheck: The oil beads at the edge of the paste
steps.videoShot: Close-up of oil glistening at the edge.

steps.title: Add water and salt
steps.text: Pour in the rest of the 100 ml water and add ¼ tsp salt. Stir.
steps.visualCue: A smooth, pourable orange curry, like thin custard
steps.cameraCheck: The curry in the pan
steps.videoShot: Water being stirred into the paste.

steps.title: Add the kokum
steps.text: Add the soaked kokum pieces and their pink soaking water.
steps.tip: Using tamarind? Squeeze the soaked tamarind, strain, and add half the water now; taste after step 20 and add more only if needed.
steps.visualCue: The curry turns a little deeper orange-pink
steps.cameraCheck: The kokum pieces in the curry
steps.videoShot: Kokum and its water going into the pan.

steps.title: Simmer the curry
steps.text: Bring to a gentle bubble on medium heat, then lower to low.
steps.tip: Taste now and fix salt and sourness; it is hard to stir much once the fish is in.
steps.visualCue: Lazy, slow bubbles; the curry tastes balanced, tangy and mildly hot
steps.cameraCheck: The gently bubbling curry
steps.videoShot: Slow bubbles breaking on the surface.

steps.title: Add the fish
steps.text: Slide the 2 marinated steaks into the curry in one layer. Spoon curry over the top. Do not stir.
steps.visualCue: The steaks are covered or half-covered with curry
steps.cameraCheck: The fish sitting in the curry
steps.videoShot: A steak being slid gently into the pan.

steps.title: Simmer the fish gently
steps.text: Cover and cook on low heat. Instead of stirring, hold the pan by its handles and swirl it once or twice.
steps.tip: Coconut milk shortcut: pour in the 60 ml coconut milk after 4 minutes, swirl, and heat just until it bubbles once; boiling hard can make coconut milk split.
steps.visualCue: The flesh turns from translucent pink to opaque white all the way through and flakes when pressed at the thickest part with a spoon
steps.cameraCheck: A steak pressed with a spoon to show white, flaky flesh
steps.videoShot: The pan being swirled gently.

steps.title: Rest and serve
steps.text: Turn off the heat and let the curry stand, covered, before serving. Remove the kokum pieces if you like (they are not usually eaten).
steps.visualCue: A thin layer of orange oil on top and the curry slightly thicker
steps.cameraCheck: The finished curry in a bowl
steps.videoShot: The curry being ladled into a bowl with one steak on top.

reasons: about 30 g of lean, high-quality protein from fish, plus omega-3 fats (surmai and especially bangda), and nothing is deep-fried. Spices, garlic, ginger and kokum add flavour without sugar. Points come off for the high saturated fat from coconut plus coconut oil (about 19 g, est.), sodium around 1,000 mg, and almost no vegetables. Restaurant versions often fry the fish first, use more oil and coconut, add more salt, and are served with a large mound of white rice.

researchRating.basis: Goan fish curry rice is the defining everyday meal of Goa and a fixture of Mumbai's Goan, Malvani and coastal restaurants; Mumbai food media (Homegrown, Culture Trip, LBB, Curly Tales) repeatedly name it among the city's must-eat Goan dishes, and celebrity chefs (Ranveer Brar, Sanjeev Kapoor) and leading Indian and international blogs (Ruchik Randhap, Raksha's Kitchen, Whisk Affair, RecipeTin Eats, with comments running to more than 10 pages) publish versions. Visible recipe star ratings were scarce (Anjum Anand's version on Yummy Tummy Aarthi: 3.67/5 from only 3 votes; Tesco Real Food's Goan-style curry has 145 ratings, but the average was not visible). Small deductions because opinions split on "authentic" fish, coconut milk and tomato, and because the fish quality makes or breaks the dish.

storage: Fridge-safe in a closed box for up to 2 days; cool it within 1 hour of cooking. Many Goan cooks say it tastes better the next day, because the fish soaks up the masala. Freezing is not recommended: the fish turns soft and watery and the coconut gravy can split (the gravy alone, without fish, freezes for up to 1 month). Reheat gently in a pan on low heat, covered, swirling the pan instead of stirring, just until it bubbles once; or microwave in 30-second bursts. Do not boil hard, as the fish will break.
leftoverRemix: Goan fish curry pulao. Lift out the leftover fish, remove any bones and flake it. Heat ½ tsp oil, fry 2 tbsp sliced onion until golden, add the leftover gravy and cook until it is thick and clinging. Add 1 cup cooked rice and the flaked fish, toss gently for 2 minutes, then finish with lime juice and chopped coriander. The coconut-kokum masala turns it into a quick tangy fish rice.
burnOff: about 6.0 km of running (420 ÷ 70 kcal/km, for a 70 kg adult), or about 8.4 km of brisk walking (about 1 hour 40 minutes at 5 km/h, using about 50 kcal/km for walking) (est.). With 150 g rice (about 615 kcal): about 8.8 km running or 12.3 km walking (est.).
